messages:
zoe: heads-up: found a tricky ctx/streaming race in the Go generator while debugging our onboarding sample.
aj: what did you see?
zoe: if the context passed to NewGenerator cancels while the handshake is pending, constructor returns but a read goroutine keeps running. reproduced reliably by adding a small artificial handshake delay in the test server.
mike: oof. can you paste the tiny repro?
zoe: sure:
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 20*time.Millisecond)
g, err := client.NewGenerator(ctx, modelID, opts...)
// immediately call g.Next() or g.Stream()
```
with a 30-50ms server-side handshake sleep the ctx often times out and we see a leftover goroutine doing network reads.
aj: thanks. sounds like we spawn the reader loop before handshake confirmation and we never cancel it on constructor error. python/js SDKs avoid this by gating the read loop until handshake completes.
mike: quick options: 1) delay spawning the read loop until handshake success; 2) spawn it but pass a childCtx you cancel on constructor failure. both are non-breaking.
zoe: I tried both locally. delaying spawn is simple and fixes the leak. creating a childCtx + cancel works too and centralizes cleanup if other code paths can error later.
aj: both are OK; prefer childCtx pattern if we want a single cancellation handle for cleanup. we should also add a unit test that simulates a slow handshake and cancels the constructor ctx to catch regressions.
mike: agreed. also update the Go SDK docs to clarify what the constructor ctx controls (handshake vs generator lifecycle). current wording is ambiguous and folks use WithTimeout in examples which is the anti-pattern here.
zoe: wrote a quick test harness that starts a fake server that sleeps during handshake, constructs with a short timeout ctx, and asserts no goroutines remain after constructor returns. will attach to PR.
aj: great. let's ship the small, non-breaking fix + test. follow up with an RFC for API ergonomics (Start/Stop or explicit lifecycle ctx) if we want a more explicit model.
mike: for samples: update onboarding and quickstarts to recommend background contexts for long-lived generators and show an explicit cancel pattern for short-lived ops. also add a linter suggestion for examples to avoid context.WithTimeout around constructors.
zoe: PR incoming: title "go: ensure generator reader is canceled if constructor ctx cancels (fix leak)". tagging @aj @mike. will include unit test + docs snippet + sample sweep checklist.

mike: thanks for catching this. small fix, high signal for DX. :thumbsup:
